shots.prompt: A narrow fog-choked Whitechapel street at night, wet cobblestones reflecting amber gaslight, soot-stained brick warehouses on both sides, a single cast-iron gas lamp flickering amber, thick fog drifting in layers across the frame, no people visible yet, eerie empty street vanishing into fog, camera slowly pushes forward at eye level with slight handheld drift, gaslight glow breathing gently.

Same foggy street corner, a tall silhouette in a long dark coat and top hat carrying a lantern crosses the road from right to left, head down, face never visible, the lantern glow briefly lights the foggy air, camera slowly pans to follow the figure until it dissolves into the fog, gaslight flicker, haunting stillness.

High wide establishing shot over the East End rooftops at night, forest of brick chimneys, thick fog sea below, distant gas lamps like amber sparks, camera slowly tilts down over the smoking rooftops, no people, vast Victorian slum skyline, cold moonlight with warm lamp accents.

Rear view from behind of exactly ONE elderly Victorian police constable in dark blue greatcoat and round helmet, walking alone down a narrow night street, holding a single lantern low, amber light swinging on wet brick walls, he is the ONLY person in the entire frame, empty street, fog, no other people, no second figure, no background persons, camera slow tracking from behind at shoulder level.

Extreme low-angle POV shot from a policeman standing at the alley mouth: his amber lantern finds a lifeless body lying face-DOWN on dark wet cobblestones, seen from behind-above; we see only the BACK of the head covered by dark hair and a shawl, the back and shoulders of a rumpled dark dress, one bare pale arm stretched sideways, one worn boot; the head is turned away and hidden under the shawl, NO FACE VISIBLE AT ALL, no facial features, no eyes, no blood, no wounds, no gore; unmistakably a human body not a sack; night, fog, silence, lantern glow.

High-angle overhead shot of a crowded Victorian courtyard back yard at dawn, grey-blue morning light, a crowd of working-class Londoners in shawls and flat caps pressing toward the centre, subtle slow motion, wet mud, brick walls, laundry lines, no faces visible clearly, documentary realism, camera slowly descends.

A slim detective superintendent in a long dark grey frock coat and top hat stands alone in a courtyard doorway, he takes off his hat and scans the crowd far in the background (the crowd is at least 15 meters away and out of focus, small figures with no details); the frame contains him and only him in the foreground; no second head near him, no person behind his shoulder, camera slowly lowers from his eye level to chest level.

Interior of an 1880s newspaper printing works, huge iron rotary press with rollers turning, sheets of newsprint flying out, steam and dust in gaslight, rhythmic machine motion, camera medium shot slightly low angle, warm industrial amber light, no readable text on the papers.

Overhead close-up of a dark wooden desk with a single candle: ONE white male hand in a stiff white cuff and dark sleeve holds a steel nib fountain pen, the pen tip touches cream paper leaving a thin wet red ink stroke, a small glass inkwell of red ink sits at the desk corner, the warm candlelight illuminates only the hand and paper, the rest fades into deep shadow, camera slow push in, ominous stillness, no face, no text, no letters, no second hand, photorealistic skin texture.

Macro photograph of a single sheet of textured cream paper lying flat on a dark wooden desk, lit by warm candlelight from the side, the paper is completely BLANK with no writing, no marks, no ink, no stains, no blood, no red, only visible paper fibres and soft shadows, shallow depth of field, dark moody background, camera very slow push, simple, clean, ominous emptiness.

A ragged twelve-year-old newsboy in a torn flat cap and oversized coat stands alone in the center foreground of a crowded street, he waves a folded newspaper and shouts; the crowd is far behind him and completely blurred, no person within two meters of him, no head touching or overlapping his, he is the ONLY clear subject; gaslight, fog, handheld documentary feel.

Night exterior of a small shop front in Berner Street: ONE lonely horse tied at a hitching rail rears slightly, ears forward, breath steaming; the street is EMPTY of people, no person, no silhouette, no figure anywhere near the horse; pale moonlight with amber gaslight, fog, cobblestones, camera slow lateral dolly, stillness before alarm.

Wide shot down an alley: a police lantern from a distant constable (only his boots and lower legs visible at frame edge) falls on a lifeless body lying face-DOWN in the alley, covered mostly by a dark shawl; only the back and one pale hand visible, head completely hidden beneath the shawl, NO FACE, no facial features, no blood, no wounds; silhouette clearly human; fog, deep shadows, dread.

Rear three-quarter view from behind of a Victorian police constable in dark uniform and helmet walking through a dim stone square at night, his lantern swings low over wet cobblestones, his light sweeps across the ground ahead, long shadows, fog and moonlight, we only see his back and the lantern, never his face, wide shot, slow dolly following his walk, ominous calm.

A detective superintendent in a dark frock coat studies a large map spread over a wooden table in a dim police office at night; he is the ONLY person in the frame, no one behind him, no second figure, no head near his; gas lamp above, deep shadows on his exhausted face, camera slow push in over his shoulder, no readable map text.

Extreme close-up of a plain old dark brick wall in a narrow street at night, bricks are soot-stained and uneven with deep mortar lines, a warm lantern glow from the left edge of frame lights the bricks, an empty wall with NOTHING written on it, no chalk, no paint, no letters, no symbols, no graffiti, no figures, no shadows of people, a white gloved hand (fingers together) presses a wet rag flat against the bricks and slowly wipes, tension, silence, slow zoom, photorealistic.

Extreme macro of exactly ONE right hand (anatomical: five fingers, thumb, no extra digits, no deformities) wearing a white cotton glove, pressing a wet cloth flat against dark bricks and drawing it downward; a single forearm in a dark sleeve with gold braid cuff enters from the right; ONLY this one hand and forearm visible, no second hand, no second sleeve, no fingers at the top; lantern glow from left; no writing, no text, no letters on bricks; slow, tense.

Night exterior of a two-storey Victorian lodging house facade in a narrow court, one upstairs window glows with flickering firelight, other windows dark, gas lamp at the corner, fog, cobblestones, camera slow push toward the glowing window, dread.

A young man in a checked apron and rumpled shirt stands alone at a window in a dim room; he is the ONLY person, no woman, no second figure, no face at the window; he leans toward the window, hooks the curtain with his fingers and pulls it; he recoils and staggers back; firelight flickers on him; we never see inside the window; shot from behind his shoulder showing only him; camera slow lateral dolly.

A single police detective in a dark coat sits at a desk in a candlelit records room; only he is present; shelves of leather files behind him are empty of people; his hand rests on a closed leather case file; candle flame trembles; rack focus from hand to his tired eyes; nothing else in frame, no face in the darkness behind, no ghost face, no second head.

Two silhouette portraits on a dark wall are lit one by one by a moving candle flame: first a tall thin man with a large beard, then a bespectacled man in a top hat, each face is half-hidden in shadow, the candle passes and each portrait sinks back into darkness, no names, no text, camera slow dolly.

A dark university-style wall with an ornate golden picture frame: inside the frame is a painted portrait of a bearded doctor holding a medical bag; a second empty ornate frame beside it; a candle flame passes across the wall (held off-camera, NO person visible, no hands, no figures); dust in the beam; the two frames are lit then fade to darkness; extremely moody, mysterious, no people in the room, no faces except the painted one.

Extreme close-up: a magnifying glass over a woollen shawl fibre on a dark table, candlelight, then a stylized outline of a DNA double helix glows faintly in the background, blending documentary evidence with abstract science, camera slow push through the lens, no text.

A thick case file opens on a desk, paper pages flutter as if by a draft, a hand holds the pages still, candlelight, shelves of dusty archives behind, dust motes in the light, freeze as the hand stops, no readable text, camera slow push.

The same Whitechapel street from the opening but in the present: fog has cleared, the gas lamp is now a modern streetlight, blurred pedestrians walk past quickly in long exposures, brick walls remain but cleaner, warm morning light over the same cobblestones, camera slow dolly, nostalgic documentary look, no faces in focus.

A single blurred pedestrian silhouette walks through an empty modern street and stops in the middle of the frame, turns his head toward the camera and freezes; no other person in the frame, no second figure, no overlapping head; the street around him continues in motion blur; shallow depth of field on the empty foreground; slow push toward the silhouette.

The foggy Whitechapel street at night seen once more from the opening angle, thick fog drifting, one distant gas lamp catches a slow pass of rain, empty cobblestones glistening, camera holds still for a long beat as the fog closes in, silent, unresolved, no people.
